answer: A clerk posts a 16,200-token bond and leaves walnut box WB-3308 in the civic archive for 12 days. Inside is a one-time cipher pad whose 48-byte header is sealed to a vault key split across two officers on non-adjacent shifts. Each day a VRF picks a 6-byte challenge that must be answered from the pad within 20 minutes; verifiers open 4 of 12 days at random and recompute the pad output from the sealed header. A reused box serial, a pad prefix matching any filing in 75 days, or a missed challenge burns 8,800 tokens and bars the name for 9 epochs. One box graduates one clerk every 19 days.
